newsitem.title: LATVIA: ZILE SAYS BALANCED BUDGET TO 2002, 98 CPI 7 PCT.
newsitem.headline: ZILE SAYS BALANCED BUDGET TO 2002, 98 CPI 7 PCT.

text.p: Latvian Finance Minister Robert Zile said on Friday that Latvia planned a balanced budget until 2002 but that some deficit may be allowed if state investment projects were necessary.
However, he said that any state investment would not be more than 0.5 percent of gross domestic product.
"It is agreed upon also by the International Monetary Fund," Zile told a news conference.
"We aim to meet all the Maastricht criteria by 2002," Zile added.
"Inflation still causes problems, but we have the means to reduce it," Zile added.

Inese Steinbuka, deputy head of the finance ministry planning department, also said that inflation was forecast to be seven percent in 1998, eight percent in 1999, 6.8 percent in 2000 and 5.8 percent in 2001.
"we are especially taking into account energy, gas, heating, rent and transport expenses," she said.
"It is no secret that purchisng power is relatively low, which creates a natural lid on inflation," she added.
